verdicts.correction: CNT, the DEPENDING ON object, is OUTSIDE group G, so §13.18.38.4 GR8a governs G's length. GR8a gives the length from the current CNT whether G is a sending or a receiving operand. Only GR8b, with the object INSIDE the group, separates them: a sending operand uses the current CNT and a receiving operand uses the maximum length. An implementation that wrongly treats identifier-1 as a RECEIVING item therefore prints exactly T1=02 T2=02 G2=BB G5=BBAAA, and the golden cannot catch it. The '05' it does catch is a GR8a (fixed-capacity) error, not a GR1 error. Fix: put the object inside the group, 01 G. 05 CNT PIC 9. 05 E PIC X OCCURS 1 TO 5 DEPENDING ON CNT. Then MOVE "5AAAAA" TO G (a receiving operand, so the maximum length 6 is used), MOVE 2 TO CNT, and the expected lines are: T1=02 (sending length 1+2 = '2AA'; the receiving/max reading gives 05), T2=03 (max reading 06), G2=2BB, and after MOVE 5 TO CNT, G5=5BBAAA (max reading 5BBBBB). Also cite §13.18.38.4 GR8b in the header.

GR5 maps literal-1..5 onto identifier-3..7. The golden pins identifier-3 (I1), identifier-4 (I3) and identifier-5 (I2). It never uses identifier-6 or identifier-7, the CONVERTING operands that GR20 reads as literal-4 and literal-5, so an implementation that trims or mis-reads CONVERTING identifier operands passes. Fix: add an 85 line to the same program: 01 CV6 PIC X(2) VALUE "A ". 01 CV7 PIC X(2) VALUE "XY". MOVE "A A AA" TO W6. INSPECT W6 CONVERTING CV6 TO CV7. DISPLAY "I4=" W6. The expected line is I4=XYXYXX: under GR20 each 'A' becomes 'X' and each space becomes 'Y', because the trailing space of CV6 takes part.

GR9a has two arms: 'neither BEFORE nor AFTER' and 'identifier-4 references a zero-length item'. The writer's own notes say the zero-length identifier-4 arm (2014+) is not exercised, so the 2014 and 2023 cells of this row are unpinned. The arm is observable on AFTER. Under GR9a a zero-length identifier-4 makes the operand take part as if no phrase were written. An implementation that treats it as 'no occurrence of literal-2' falls into GR9c ('never eligible') and prints 00. Fix: add a 2014 golden with 01 ZG. 05 ZE PIC X OCCURS 0 TO 1 DEPENDING ON ZC. (ZC PIC 9 VALUE 0 outside ZG, so ZG is zero-length per §13.18.38.4 GR8a), MOVE "ABC" TO W3, INSPECT W3 TALLYING N FOR CHARACTERS AFTER INITIAL ZG giving Z1=03, and with BEFORE INITIAL ZG giving Z2=03. The 85 lines I re-derived and agree with: N1 B1-B4 A1-A7. B5=00 depends on reading 'participates only in those comparison cycles that involve that portion' as requiring the whole compared span to lie inside the region. That reading is the natural one and the GnuCOBOL/IBM behaviour, so I accept it, but the header should say that it rests on that reading.

GR16 makes ALL, FIRST and LEADING transitive. R1-R4 pin FIRST and ALL, and the ALL/FIRST ending of each other's reach, but no operand follows a LEADING. An implementation where a bare operand after LEADING takes ALL (or the default) passes. Fix: add to the 85 program MOVE "AABA" TO W4. INSPECT W4 REPLACING LEADING "A" BY "X" "B" BY "Y". DISPLAY "R5=" W4. The expected line is R5=XXBA. By transitivity "B" is LEADING. Its first eligible comparison cycle began at position 1, where 'B' does not match, so under GR17c no occurrence of 'B' is leading. Positions 1-2 are the contiguous leading 'A's, and the 'A' at position 4 is not contiguous. If 'B' took ALL instead, the line would be XXYA. Note that the LEADING consumer defect GR-14.9.22.4-L2.2 involves AFTER anchoring, which this line does not use.

all_upheld_flag: Four rows overturned: GR1, GR5, GR9 and GR16. I re-derived every output line of the four programs by hand from GR8, GR9, GR12, GR17 and GR20 before comparing with the .out files, and every line of the .out files is correct. The overturns are about coverage and discrimination, not values. For GR1, I checked §13.18.38.4 GR8 and found that sending and receiving lengths differ only when the ODO object is inside the group. For GR5, GR9 and GR16, I listed every arm of the rule text and found one unpinned arm in each (identifier-6/7, zero-length identifier-4, LEADING transitivity). For K4 and K6 (BACKWARD, 2+-character literals), I tried both readings of the comparison window at the rightmost position (NOTE 2), and both give 02 and AXY. For K1, I checked 'first occurrence in the direction of the scan' against the NOTE 1 worked example. For B4 (BEFORE boundary fixed before cycle 1) and F2/R4 (GR17d, each FIRST separately), the alternative readings give different output, so these lines discriminate. For editions, only BACKWARD forces the 2023 directory, and the other three programs use 85 syntax. I ran cite.py --check on all 20 citations and all returned OK.
